E1.evidence: The issue is filed under '## Feature request' and asks to 'discuss declaring a dependency on the LTTng userspace tracer (LTTng-UST) on Linux'. It describes a deliberate packaging choice ('This LTTng dependency isn't declared. This was initially for simplicity ... and because of some concerns about overhead.') rather than a concrete defect with a reproducer or error log; the maintainer response treats it as a request ('I think that having the tracepoints available by default is a reasonable request.').

E2.evidence: The resolving changes are dependency declaration and build configuration: ros2_tracing#31 edits tracetools/package.xml, tracetools/CMakeLists.txt, config.h.in, CI workflows and README to 'explicitly depend on/expect LTTng-UST on Linux'; ros2/ci#690 installs LTTng packages in the CI Dockerfiles; rosdistro#36641 adds an 'lttng-tools' rosdep rule for RHEL; ros2_tracing#48 adds an explicit dl link. No unit's declared interface changes. rmw_fastrtps#591 (merged 2022-03-21) only adds tracetools instrumentation calls to rmw_fastrtps_cpp and ros2_documentation#2877 adds a build-with-tracing guide ('This guide will become invalid/unneeded if we do https://github.com/ros2/ros2/issues/1177'); neither changes an interface between units. The issue author closed it with 'The PRs have been merged, so I'm closing this.'

E3.evidence: No failing operation between two units is documented; the request concerns whether tracepoints are compiled into binaries by default.

E4.evidence: No interaction failure is documented; the effect described is that the tracing feature 'currently isn't available out-of-the-box'.

ineligible_reason: Not a concrete defect (E1 fails: feature request); on the E2 tree it stops at step 4, build (dependency declaration, rosdep rule, CI install only).
